text:
Alex K.: @here quick follow-up on where we put the dequant fusion and how kernels should advertise quant support. tl;dr: we need a clear contract so routing + fallback logic stays simple.
Priya N.: agree. main options: 1) runtime does dequant then calls existing fp kernels, 2) kernels accept quant inputs and internally fuse dequant, 3) hybrid (partial fusion + small runtime shim). tradeoffs?
Jordan M.: option 2 gives best perf (no memcpy) but means kernel API grows. option 1 is simplest for rollout and backwards compatible.
Samira L.: perf numbers from the POC: INT8-attn with kernel-fusion = ~1.9x token/s vs runtime-dequant path. latency p50 improved ~18ms on our 8k context benchmark.
Alex K.: ok but kernel API growth is scary. specifically we'd need to expose: input_dtype, scale/meta per-tensor, qlayout descriptor, and a flag for fused-kv-cache layout. that's 3-4 new fields on call contract.
Priya N.: Right. Also need capability discovery: kernel registry should expose something like `supports_quant: [\"INT8\",\"FP8\",\"INT4\"]` and `fusion_level: \"none|partial|full\"` so router can pick.
Jordan M.: proposal: keep kernel callsite minimal by packing quant metadata into a single small header blob: `quant_hdr_v1` (16-32 bytes) so we don't keep adding args. kernel impls can parse it.
Samira L.: that helps ABI stability. but we must version that blob. suggestion: header = {version, dtype, scale_ptr, layout_code, flags}. runtime provides pointer/index into shared metadata buffer.
Alex K.: memory safety note: pointer/index means shared memory across processes if private deploys use multi-process. better to make it an index into an RPC-attached metadata block, not raw pointers.
eng-runtime-bot: reminder: RFC follow-up meeting scheduled Thu 10am. Agenda: kernel header format, registry API, rollout plan.
Priya N.: edge case: cached KV already quantized for memory savings. If kernel expects floats but runtime dequants, we lose cached memory benefit. So if we do runtime-dequant path, need an on-the-fly reclaim plan.
Jordan M.: another operational thing: fallback sequence. I propose router tries: (1) model->preferred_quant_kernel if supports, (2) compatible lower-precision kernel, (3) runtime-dequant->fp kernel. That keeps perf without risking failures.
Samira L.: +1. But also add a quick admittance check: kernel must declare `max_seq_len` and `kv_layout` because some quant kernels currently don't support packed kv.
Alex K.: rollout plan suggestion:
- Phase 0: kernel registry fields + simple `quant_hdr_v1` no-op implementation in existing kernels
- Phase 1: opt-in fused quant kernels for INT8/FP8 on certain architectures, router prefers them
- Phase 2: telemetry + auto-fallback thresholds (if perf regresses >5% revert to runtime-dequant)
Priya N.: tests: add unit for header parsing, integration for fallback order, e2e perf tests (8k/16k), and correctness fuzz (random scales, layout permutations).
Jordan M.: implementation detail: where to place fusion code? I'd like a small common lib inside runtime/kernels/common so both CUDA and ROCm builds can share header parsing and quant util routines.
Samira L.: agree. also add a CI job that validates kernel ABI across builds (cuda/rocm/x86) to catch regressions early.
Alex K.: action items:
- Priya: write kernel registry patch w/ fields + example manifest (due Mon)
- Jordan: prototype `quant_hdr_v1` binary blob + parser in common lib (due Wed)
- Samira: perf microbench harness for INT4/INT8/FP8 attn (due next Fri)
- Me: update router to consult `supports_quant` and implement fallback order (start Tue)
Priya N.: noted. i'll include an example model manifest snippet:
```
"model_manifest": {
  "id": "redwood-quant-test",
  "preferred_quant": "INT8",
  "kernel_capabilities": {
    "supports_quant": ["INT8","FP8"],
    "fusion_level": "full",
    "max_seq_len": 8192
  }
}
```
Alex K.: one more: we need a small telemetry event for each fallback so we can compute frequency and trigger rollbacks automatically if new kernels cause >2% error rate or >10% perf hit.
eng-runtime-bot: note created: TICKET-4821 \"quant-kernel-registry-and-router\" assigned to Priya N.
Jordan M.: I'll sync with infra about shared metadata buffer semantics for private deployments.
Samira L.: cool. if no objections i'll merge registry branch after Priya's patch lands and we have the header spec.
Alex K.: no objections from me. thanks everyone :rocket:
